BOL5

GeometryCircles
Game: This is a picture to explore: drag the point C and watch the two circles beside the tall line stay the same size.
How to play: Drag C with a mouse or finger, or focus it and use the arrow keys. Press Show hint for the proof lines and Check the claim for the answer.
Look for the math

Archimedes' fifth lemma draws a circle on each side of the upright line through C. They look different, because one leans into the left semicircle and the other into the right, but they are exactly the same size. Drag C to see it, then read why.

The figure

AB is the diameter of the big semicircle. C is any point on AB, and CD goes straight up from C. Inside the big semicircle sit two more semicircles, one with diameter AC and one with diameter CB. Together they form the shape Archimedes called the arbelos. Each little circle touches the upright line CD, one tangent circle on the left and one on the right.

The radius that fits

Write AC = 2r₁, CB = 2r₂ and the radius of a little circle as r. Because C lies on AB, the big radius is r₁ + r₂. A circle of radius r whose centre is r from CD and 2√(r₁r) above AB touches CD, the small semicircle and the big semicircle all at once; the same calculation on the other side uses r₂. It works exactly when

1 / r = 1 / r₁ + 1 / r₂  that is  r = r₁ r₂ / (r₁ + r₂).

So r is half the harmonic mean of r₁ and r₂. The left and right circles use the same r₁ and r₂, just swapped, so their radii are equal. The logic test checks all three tangencies and this formula at hundreds of positions of C, including tilted and rescaled diameters.

The diameter HE

Let E be where the left circle touches CD and H the far end of its diameter. Then HE = 2r, and substituting the formula above gives

AC · CB = AB · HE.

The right circle gives the same product, so its diameter equals HE too: the two circles are equal, as Archimedes' Book of Lemmas, Proposition 5, says. The hint draws the straight lines of his proof, which link the touch points to the ends A and B. One quirk of the old Java applet is kept: its hint labels the crossing of those lines "D" as well as the top of the upright line, but the claim is about the circles, not that label.

Try dragging C close to A or B: both circles shrink to nothing together. Drag it to the middle: they grow to the same largest size.
